assets.prompt:
Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: EIGHT-panel raster microscopy-inspired stage atlas for a biology exploration game. Precisely FOUR columns by TWO rows, eight equal SQUARE tiles. Whole image aspect 2:1, preferred 2048x1024. NO margins, NO gutters, NO border lines, NO labels, numbers, text, scales, arrows or watermark. Each tile a separate complete view with the subject within its central 72%, nothing crosses tile boundaries.
Primary request: an independently composed eight-stage educational reconstruction of the early sexual myxomycete life cycle, followed by gradually spreading plasmodium and sparse vein formation. NOT a documentary time series and NOT a species identification key. The organism remains ONE continuous cell after fusion, not a colony of joined separate cells.
Style: photorealistic natural transmitted-light optical microscopy appearance, slightly uneven neutral illumination, restrained grey-cream colour, fine granular translucent cytoplasm, softly focused tiny detritus, natural imperfect organic contours. Nuclei are darker muted grey roundish internal structures and clearly distinguishable from the much smaller cytoplasmic granules. No cartoon outline, no rendered glass, no CGI jelly or gel droplets, no glowing rims, no decorative bubbles, no jewel-like spores or perfect spheres.
Eight tiles in exact reading order:
TOP LEFT 1: one finely textured nearly round spore wall opens with one tiny irregular amoeboid cell emerging; restrained subtle roughness, not exaggerated spines, no ornate diagnostic netting.
TOP SECOND 2: two clearly SEPARATE motile forms in the same optical field: one uneven lobed amoeba with one nucleus and one elongated swimmer with one nucleus and two delicate flagella. They are alternatives, not a dividing cell.
TOP THIRD 3: two compatible lobed cells beginning to fuse, their unequal lobes touching via a short narrow cytoplasmic bridge. One nucleus in each lobe, TWO nuclei total. This fusion silhouette must be unmistakably different from tile5, which is a unified broad cell.
TOP RIGHT 4: a SINGLE compact irregular oval zygote after nuclear fusion, exactly ONE distinct nucleus inside it. No bridge, no split, no wall between cells.
BOTTOM LEFT 5: same cell now somewhat larger and broadly oval with shallow uneven margins, exactly TWO clearly separated nuclei in ONE uninterrupted cytoplasm; no cleavage furrow or waist, no septum, no joining pair of lobes. It is nuclear division without cell division.
BOTTOM SECOND 6: a larger young plasmodium, ONE cell with exactly FOUR visible nuclei and several short broad irregular pseudopodial lobes. No dense mature network yet. The four are an explanatory count, not a mature organism's nucleus limit.
BOTTOM THIRD 7: wider field of the same organism spreading out into a broad asymmetrical thin sheet with generous rounded lobes, ONE continuous cytoplasm, no separate amoebae. More numerous much smaller nuclei are now only faint internal granules, NOT four large balls. Show growth and scale transition, still mainly a sheet with NO complex vein network.
BOTTOM RIGHT 8: same broadened sheet begins forming a few connected thicker cytoplasmic channels, only three or four sparse branching paths and one or two joining loops, joined to broad expanding margins. Continuous living cytoplasm throughout, not separate worms, roots or independent cells. Substantial open spaces but not yet a dense mature mesh. Small nuclei no longer individually emphasized at this wider scale.
Biological continuity: tiles4–8 have related irregular contours that spread progressively rather than suddenly changing into another object; each step is visibly distinct even at phone size. Same illumination and medium across all eight panels. Magnification changes are explanatory, not measured; no invented labels or species-specific microscopic diagnostic characters.
Plate identity: Badhamia polycephala (synonym Physarum polycephalum). This is a distinct composition for this species' educational route, not a claim its early microscopic cells have uniquely identifiable anatomy. Composition variations for this plate: neutral pale grey-beige transmitted field; cell emerges toward lower right; amoeba lies left of diagonally upward swimmer; fusion lies diagonally lower-left to upper-right; compact zygote is a slightly triangular oval; spreading cell extends a broad scalloped fan toward the upper right; sparse vein paths make an asymmetric fork opening upper right. Render all eight panels as newly composed subjects, not recolours or repeated crops.
